title: Understanding the Components
text: The expected squared error can be broken down into three main components: the variance of the noise, the squared bias, and the variance of the model. Can you identify which part of the equation represents each of these components?

title: Focus on the Noise Term
text: The term $${\sigma}^2$$ represents the variance of the noise in the data. This is a constant that reflects the inherent randomness in the data generation process. How does this affect the overall error?

title: Identifying the Bias Term
text: Which part of the equation represents the squared bias?

title: Variance of the Model
text: The term E[(E[f_hat_theta(x)]-f_hat_theta(x))**2] represents the variance of the model. This term captures the variability of the model predictions around their expected value. How does this contribute to the overall error?
